2609.02270.title: CrashDiffuser: VLM-Guided Collision Intent Reasoning for Fine-Grained Safety-Critical Traffic Scenario Generation
2609.02270.paper_summary: Generating safety-critical scenarios is essential for evaluating autonomous driving systems. However, existing generators primarily focus on inducing collisions and offer limited control over where contact occurs on the target vehicle. In this paper, we study fine-grained safety-critical scenario generation, where success requires both a target collision and a specified head, rear, or side contact region. We propose CrashDiffuser, a closed-loop VLM-guided diffusion framework that decouples semantic collision reasoning from continuous trajectory synthesis through a hierarchical collision-intent interface derived from the requested target contact region. At initialization, the VLM extracts reusable scene-level context; at each replanning step, it predicts a structured action tuple describing speed change, turning behavior, and collision stage. This intent conditions a diffusion model to generate executable adversarial trajectories, while collision-guided sampling, candidate selection, and short-horizon replanning adapt generation to the target vehicle's evolving behavior. On WOMD-derived closed-loop scenarios, CrashDiffuser achieves a target-collision rate of 50.33% in a single attempt and 67.98% after three attempts, together with a contact-region control success rate of 40.05% and competitive trajectory naturalness. Component ablations further support the proposed design.
2609.02270.paper_summary_zh: 生成安全關鍵場景對於評估自動駕駛系統至關重要。<lb/>然而，現有的生成器主要集中在誘發碰撞上，並且對於目標車輛上接觸發生的位置控制有限。<lb/>在本文中，我們研究了細粒度的安全關鍵場景生成，其中成功需要同時實現目標碰撞和指定的前部、後部或側面接觸區域。<lb/>我們提出了CrashDiffuser，一個閉環VLM引導的擴散框架，通過從請求的目標接觸區域派生的分層碰撞意圖接口，將語義碰撞推理與連續軌跡合成解耦。<lb/>在初始化時，VLM提取可重用的場景級上下文；在每次重新規劃步驟中，它預測一個結構化的動作元組，描述速度變化、轉向行為和碰撞階段。<lb/>這個意圖使擴散模型能夠生成可執行的對抗性軌跡，而碰撞引導的採樣、候選選擇和短期重新規劃則使生成適應目標車輛不斷變化的行為。<lb/>在基於WOMD的閉環場景中，CrashDiffuser在一次嘗試中實現了50.33%的目標碰撞率，並在三次嘗試後達到了67.98%，同時接觸區域控制成功率為40.05%，且軌跡自然性具有競爭力。<lb/>組件消融進一步支持了所提出的設計。
